description: Constitution of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (Proclamation No. 1/1995)

articles.title: Scope of Application and Interpretation
articles.summary: All federal and state legislative, executive and judicial organs have the responsibility to respect and enforce the provisions of this Chapter.

articles.title: Right of Persons Arrested
articles.summary: Persons arrested have the right to be informed promptly of the reasons for their arrest and any charges against them in a language they understand.

articles.title: Right of Accused Persons
articles.summary: Accused persons have the right to a public trial by an ordinary court of law within a reasonable time, to be presumed innocent until proven guilty, and to full legal representation.

articles.title: Right to Equality
articles.summary: All persons are equal before the law and are entitled without any discrimination to the equal protection of the law.

articles.title: Right of Access to Justice
articles.summary: Everyone has the right to bring a justiciable matter to, and to obtain a decision or judgment by, a court of law or any other competent body with judicial power.

articles.title: Right to Property
articles.summary: Every Ethiopian citizen has the right to the ownership of private property, including the right to acquire, use, and dispose of property.

chapters.chapter: Chapter 9: Structure and Powers of the Courts

articles.title: Independence of the Judiciary
articles.summary: An independent judiciary is established by the Constitution. Supreme Federal judicial authority is vested in the Federal Supreme Court.

articles.title: Judicial Powers
articles.summary: Judicial powers, both at Federal and State levels, are vested in the courts. Courts of any level shall be free from any interference of any state organ or any other authority.

articles.title: Jurisdiction of Courts & Cassation Division
articles.summary: The Federal Supreme Court has the highest and final judicial authority. The Federal Supreme Court has a power of cassation over any final court decision containing a fundamental error of law.

description: Criminal Code of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia

articles.title: Principle of Legality
articles.summary: No one shall be punished for an act or omission which was not defined as an offense by law at the time when it was committed.

articles.title: Principal Offender & Accomplices
articles.summary: A person who commits a crime by himself or through an intermediary is liable as a principal offender.

chapters.chapter: Book 5: Crimes Against Property & Financial Crimes

articles.title: Theft and Misappropriation
articles.summary: Whoever intentionally takes another person's movable property without consent with intent to appropriate it is punishable with rigorous imprisonment.

articles.title: Fraud and Deceitful Misrepresentation
articles.summary: Whoever intentionally misleads another person by deceptive statements or concealment of material facts to obtain an unlawful financial gain is punishable with rigorous imprisonment and fine.

articles.title: Breach of Trust & Embezzlement
articles.summary: Whoever, having received money, documents, or property in trust, misappropriates or uses them for personal benefit contrary to trust commitments commits breach of trust.

chapters.chapter: Book 6: Crimes Against the Public & State

articles.title: Abuse of Power by Public Servants
articles.summary: Any public official who intentionally uses their office to procure an improper advantage or cause injury to the rights of another commits a federal offense.

articles.title: Perjury and False Testimony Before Court
articles.summary: Whoever gives false testimony, false statements, or submits forged evidence in judicial proceedings is punishable under rigorous penal terms.

description: The Civil Code regulating Contracts, Obligations, Property, and Tort

articles.title: Definition of Contract
articles.summary: A contract is an agreement whereby two or more persons as between themselves create, vary or extinguish obligations of a proprietary nature.

articles.title: Binding Nature of Contracts
articles.summary: The provisions of a contract lawfully formed shall be binding on the parties as though they were law.

articles.title: Effects of Non-Performance
articles.summary: Where a party does not perform their contractual obligations, the other party may demand performance, cancel the contract, or claim damages for non-performance.

articles.title: Damages and Compensation
articles.summary: The party who fails to perform shall be liable to pay damages for loss caused to the other party as a direct consequence of non-performance.

articles.title: Force Majeure Standard
articles.summary: Force majeure results from an unforeseeable and insurmountable occurrence that makes performance of contractual obligations absolutely impossible.

articles.title: Source of Tort Liability
articles.summary: Whoever causes damage to another by fault commits an offense and is liable to make good the damage.

articles.title: Modes of Reparation
articles.summary: The court shall award damages in cash or in kind to place the injured party in the position they would have been in had the tort not occurred.

description: The Revised Commercial Code of the FDRE

articles.title: Definition of Commercial Activities
articles.summary: Persons who professionally and for gain carry on commercial activities, supply of goods, services, or financial intermediation are deemed traders.

articles.title: Duties of Commercial Registry & Disclosure
articles.summary: All commercial business entities must register corporate standing and maintain verifiable statutory books.

chapters.chapter: Book 3: Negotiable Instruments and Banking Transactions

articles.title: Dishonored Cheques & Commercial Paper
articles.summary: Drawing a negotiable cheque without sufficient funds or stopping payment unlawfully establishes strict commercial and civil liability.

description: The Labor Law of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia

articles.title: Unlawful Termination of Contract
articles.summary: Termination of an employment contract without lawful grounds under this Proclamation entitles the worker to reinstatement or statutory severance compensation.

articles.title: Severance Pay Calculation
articles.summary: Severance compensation standards payable upon lawful or unlawful contract cessation based on service duration.

description: Proclamation to Re-Determine the Powers and Jurisdiction of Federal Courts

articles.title: Jurisdiction of Federal First Instance Court
articles.summary: The Federal First Instance Court has jurisdiction over civil cases where the claim does not exceed 10,000,000 Birr, and criminal offenses with penalty not exceeding 15 years imprisonment.

articles.title: Jurisdiction of Federal High Court
articles.summary: The Federal High Court has jurisdiction over civil claims exceeding 10,000,000 Birr, international commercial arbitrations, patent disputes, and serious federal criminal matters.

articles.title: Jurisdiction of Federal Supreme Court & Cassation
articles.summary: The Federal Supreme Court has jurisdiction on appellate matters from the Federal High Court, and sits with 5 judges in the Cassation Division to determine fundamental errors of law.
